Hello everyone, just a little bit about me!

I was first introduced to the bass guitar when I was about 9 or so and played in the school band, after some time of that my parents had bought me a Yamaha electric guitar followed by a Hohner acoustic guitar and I played then for many years to come. (I still have the Hohner, it's in pretty terrible shape now though.)

I spent a little bit of time in the school choir and learned that I love singing even more than I love playing guitar.

Fast-forward to age 16 or so and I had been going to my older brother's band practices (metal band, they were very well-known locally, you can PM me if you are curious which band) and just absorbed the music and talent from him and their singer(s).

Quickly thereafter I learned I can not just sing but also scream, and not to toot my own horn but it just so happened I had a real talent for being a metal singer. So I would practice with them in the event their singer did not show up.

Fast-forward again to age 19 where me and my life long best friend who just so happened to be an amazing drummer decided we were going to start ''jamming'' together with me playing guitar.

It wasn't long after that we found someone who would then play guitar for us so that I could focus on singing and writing lyrics, and we did, and it was terrible! Haha

Another year to a year and a half our guitarist friend had moved away and we replaced him with another, actually better guitarist, who somewhat knew what he was doing, and from there we grew, we found a bass player, and we played glorious metal music for the next 6-7 years after that (we replaced that guitarist a couple years down the road) but it was an amazing experience being well received at all of our shows, in general, playing at all the bars, participating in battle of the bands, it was an amazing ride, but alas all good things must come to an end and it did.

We had a falling out with the guitarist and were never able to pick up the pieces of our broken band.

So that's my story, I haven't really played music with anyone else in about 2 years now. I'm a metal head but I also grew up listening to classic rock so I have a great love for the rock scene as well and have always tried to keep an open mind about music.

TL;DR Hi, I'm the creator of this sub and just wanted you to know I have a musical history! Much experience on stage, I mostly listen to metal but always keep an open mind, I also have some very close friends and relatives who are all musically gifted and play all different genres of music.

Our modern western way of life is vastly different than it was a mere generation or two ago. Sometime in the post-war world, the baby boomers of the democratic west decided that things weren't good enough. Blacks in America were still largely stripped of their rights while being gay was practically illegal. So people organized and fought, spurred on in America by the Vietnam War and here in Canada by the American influence (20,000 - 30,000 US hippy draft-dodgers flooded Canada and brought their social revolution with them).

While the gains made for minority rights, particularly for blacks, were good and just, some of the more questionable aspects of that social revolution are still with us today. One of those is the concept of moral relativism, which I believe is the cause for the decline of the once great civilization the west was building.

Moral relativism is the belief that there is no natural right and wrong and good or evil. Instead, adherents to moral relativism believe that right are wrong are subjective to the time, place, culture and even the individual themselves. For instance, one person believes eating pork is okay, another person may believe it is wrong, and therefore both are right. There is no "right" answer, as the individual culture determines what is right and wrong. Morality, then, is relative to time, place and person. This has been the guiding principle of our western society, from the US to Europe to Australia to Canada, for the past 50 or so years.

Moral relativism has grown so strong since the days of the hippy revolution that it is now the predominant culture. Our courts have enshrined relativism in our laws, often without the consent of the electorate. Here in Canada we have so-called "Human Rights Tribunals" which have taken moral relativism to the extreme by punishing people for even insulting the feelings of others! In their belief, the feelings of a person are relative to their perception of reality, and thus are a protected human right!

The opposite of moral relativism is moral absolutism. This was the default morality of society until the 1960's and 70's.

In a nutshell, moral absolutism claims that no matter who you are, where you are or what you think, there are set of unbreakable rules that applies to all humanity. Sometimes called natural law, absolutism maintains that nature, or God, or whomever, has a set of laws that define good and bad, right and wrong. An example would be murder: every society, regardless of their culture, religion, ethical makeup, etc holds murder to be an evil act and a punishable act. While laws have been written to describe punishments for murder, it is instinctive to sane people the world over that murder is wrong. This is a natural law, or a moral absolute.

The Book of Exodus contains 10 moral absolutes, known as the 10 Commandments, which include murder, theft, lying, rape and disrespecting one's parents as acts which are just simply wrong. Likewise, even Buddhism contains some moral absolutes, recognizing rape and murder and theft as great wrongs.

Unfortunately, not all religions recognize the same absolutes. Socialism in Russia and China was okay with murder, kidnapping and theft to achieve its ends. Feminism has no problem with lying, manipulating and even physically harming in order to get its message across. All three of these movements uphold moral relativism, and not absolutism, as their defining feature.

Feminism and socialism have altered the western world to the point where today relativism is the default morality. Just look at the way young men and women behave, with sexual promiscuity, glorifying in violence and crudeness, and showing complete disrespect for the very society that gave them life.

Relativism is the reason the abortion debate will never be settled. It is the reason why military interventions, especially by the US, is seen as okay regardless of the reason. Relativism is the reason there is so much violence, and the reason so many people are willing to be offended at the slightest mistake and run off to a "Human Rights" tribunal or court house.

I used to believe in relativism, parroting former Prime-Minister Pierre Trudeau's famous quote that "Your freedom ends where my nose begins." In high school and in college my teachers fed me the concept that morality is what I make of it; all but one professor. I don't remember his name, but he was my first year political sciences prof and he refused to be a liberal academic. He wasn't conservative, either. He held a faith in the profession of an academic, and tried to just give us the facts and let our young minds figure out the politics. He was also very critical of modern society's moral compass.

After years without a rudder, believing that whatever I felt at the time was right must be so, I have changed. I now know that indeed, some things are absolute. I personally believe that these are grave laws of living given to us from God (a God that is all all good and therefore anything that is against God is bad), but I don't expect everybody to have the same faith as me. It would be good enough if people accepted these universal absolutes as is, whether they believe they come from God or the Cosmos or even from elves. These moral absolutes not only provide a firm foundation for society to function, but they also provide a rudder and a course for society to take, giving us strength and confidence in our daily decisions, our politics and our identities.

To finish, I would like to list some of these moral absolutes as I've come to learn them, through my studies of the Bible, of philosophy, of history (which I studied in college) and of economics.

Do not murder Do not steal Do not lie Do not willfully harm or torture other living souls Do not covet what others have Do not defile your own body or soul
